conflicts.fact: Value of the mkokoteni's acceleration / g used across the sequence
conflicts.versions: L2: a = 2 m/s² and says gravitational acceleration will be found in L4; L3: a = 2.5 m/s² ('from previous lesson's estimate' though L2 used 2); L4: g = 9.8 m/s²; L5: g = 10 m/s² (while saying L4 gave 'roughly 10'); L7: a = 10 m/s²; L8: a ≈ 3 m/s² (slope component). The cart's acceleration is presented as 2, 2.5, 3, 9.8 and 10 m/s² with no reconciliation.

conflicts.fact: Cart speed and distance after 8 s
conflicts.versions: L3 says approximately 20 m/s and 80 m after 8 s (a = 2.5 gives 20 m/s and 80 m, which is internally consistent), whereas L2's diagram gives 16 m/s at 8 s with a = 2 (distance 64 m); L8 with a = 3 gives 24 m/s at 8 s.

conflicts.fact: Cart speed and distance by time/distance on the escarpment
conflicts.versions: L4: after 3 s v = 29.4 m/s, s = 44.1 m (free fall at 9.8); L5: after 5 s v = 50 m/s and s = 125 m, and v ≈ 100 m/s at 500 m; L8: crash-point speed approx 40 m/s (144 km/h), and 34.6 m/s at 200 m with a = 3. Also L5 says point B (200 m) is about 5 s after release, but 200 m would give v = 63 m/s while s = 125 m at 5 s; inconsistent with its own checkpoint.

L2 says 'acceleration means a constant change in velocity' whereas acceleration is generally the rate of change of velocity (L1 defines it as increasing speed); L2 and L4 use constant acceleration framing differently.

conflicts.fact: Whether the cart on the slope accelerates at g
conflicts.versions: L4 and L5 treat the cart's acceleration as g (free rolling, 9.8/10 m/s²) and L7 uses a = 10; L8 says only a slope component acts so the cart's acceleration (3 m/s²) is less than g and says free fall is the limiting case; L4 DQB also asks whether a non-vertical road gives 9.8.

conflicts.fact: Number of equations of linear motion
conflicts.versions: L2, L3, L7, L8 refer to four equations; L5 and L6 refer to three equations (v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as).

conflicts.fact: Drop experiment data heights and class value of g
conflicts.versions: L4 drops all objects from exactly 2 m; L5 says L4 data covered h = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 m, and says g values cluster 9.8–10.2 while L4 says average close to 9.8 and L5's teacher says about 10.

L3 boda-boda from 15 m/s braking in 45 m gives a = 2.5 m/s²; L6 uses a standard braking value of 8 m/s² (matatu); not contradictory by itself but L3 asks if the cart could stop with the boda-boda deceleration vs a standard NTSA value.
